utterances.text: Could you please turn to page 7 of this document, where we can see the signature and the stamp of the person who signed this document. Is this a stamp of the Krajina government? And next to the stamp does it not state "President of the SAO Krajina government, Dr. Milan Babic," and is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please turn to the next page, page 8 of this document. Does it not state here that this document was delivered to the United Nations, under 1, to the Council of Ministers of the European Union; under 2, 3 to the parliament of the European Community; under 4, to the High Commission of the OSCE; 5, to the Presidency of the SFRY; 6, to the Federal Executive Council; 7, to the National Assembly of the Republic of Serbia; 8, to the president of the Republic of Serbia; and 9, to the government of the Republic of Serbia? Is this what it states on page 8, Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document as a Defence exhibit, and could the document be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence and may it please --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. The document is admitted into evidence, and may it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number 236, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, the first paragraph on page 1 of this document -- and could we please have the page 1 on the monitor now. And can we look at the first paragraph under the heading. Does it not state that: "The government of the Serbian autonomous region of Krajina, at a meeting held on the 5th of September, 1991, considered the declaration on Yugoslavia adopted at an extraordinary ministerial meeting on European political cooperation in Brussels on the 27th of August, 1991, agreement on cease-fire and memorandum on an observer mission, and that in relation to those three documents takes the following position." Does that not -- does this first paragraph not state what I have just said?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: And does it not state in paragraph 2 that: "The Serbian people of SAO Krajina, who comprise the historical and ethnic territory of the Serbian people through their legal and legitimate institutions and organs, from the very beginning of their struggle for freedom and national and human dignity, who were attacked by the Croatian neo-fascist authorities, used the basic democratic means, a referendum, using their right to self-determination, the Serbian people irrevocably decided not to live in any Croatian state." Does that not -- does not the first paragraph -- this paragraph state what I have just read, Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: And the last sentence of the second paragraph, the very end, does it not state as follows: "The Serbian people of the Krajina have decided to build their sovereignty into a state in which other parts of the Serbian people in the Balkans will also live"?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at page 2, and could we have paragraph 1 displayed. What does this first paragraph say? Does say that: "All our democratic decisions that were derived from the democratic will of the Serb people of Krajina were denied by the Croatian neo-fascist authorities with arguments of violence and arms, and that unfortunately some members of the European Community at first gave tacit support and later on even open support to the Croatian neo-fascist regime." Is that what it says, Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Is that a text that you compiled, together with the government?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 2, does it say -- on this page 2, that is, which says 829, actually, on the top of the page, doesn't it say in the second paragraph that: "The Croatian neo-fascist authorities are in certain ways identical to the previous communist totalitarianism, and by destroying Yugoslavia, they wanted to force us to reconcile ourselves with terror"? And then the next sentence -- or, rather, in the next sentence you say: "In such circumstances, the denial of our referendums, our equal right, we did not have any other choice but to respond to arms by arms. The new Croatia attacked with arms our right and our decisions with the intention of forcing by way of aggression the Serb people to live in independent neo-fascist Croat state, a state which is so reminiscent of that genocidal time from 1941 to 1945." Is that what is written in the second paragraph, Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Do you say in the third paragraph that the European Community -- actually, I'm omitting a longish sentence. I'm just going to point out the gist of it. Declarations on Yugoslavia denying the Serb people right to self-determination. In the declaration on Yugoslavia, it is stated that the member countries of the European Community, "wish to remind those who are responsible for violence to their -- of their decision never to recognise changes of borders that were not achieved through peaceful means and by way of agreement." On page 3, after this, do you, as the government of Krajina, draw the attention of the European Community to the fact that these are no state borders? Is that what is written in that text, Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 3, in paragraph 3, you say that it is stated in the declaration that: "The absolutely wrong policy of Serb irregular formations that try to resolve problems that are anticipated by military means, and also, the government of the SAO Krajina does not accept this qualification for the following reasons: "1. Serb armed forces in the SAO Krajina, which consist of the police of the Krajina and the Territorial Defence of Krajina, are absolutely legal formations and are part of the single system of defence in Yugoslavia." Is that what is stated in paragraph 1, Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 2, it says that: "The Serb armed forces do not have any policy of their own but, rather, they function within the framework of and according to the programme of the policy of the government of the SAO Krajina and other institutions and organs of the SAO Krajina. The government of the SAO Krajina uses its armed forces only for the defence of its territory and its borders." Is that what is written at the end of page 3, Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: On page 4, under number 3, you say, around the middle of the paragraph: "The Serb people decided by way of a plebiscite to live in the same state with other Serbs in the territory of Yugoslavia. It is another question altogether that these decisions are being challenged by way of armed aggression, which was -- which was totally unprovoked and totally unjustified and was carried out by Croatian neo-fascist authorities. The assessment presented in the declaration that some elements of the JNA are rendering active support to the Serb side do not correspond to the truth. The truth is that the JNA takes active part in keeping the conflicting sides apart, and that in this role that it plays it is regularly attacked by the Croatian aggressors and is therefore compelled to defend itself." Is that what is written on this page number 4, Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: In the one but last paragraph on this page number 4, do you not say: "Furthermore, the decisive position taken by the European Community not to recognise any changes of borders by force constitutes major support for us in a situation when the newly established border between the SAO Krajina and the Republic of Croatia, a border established by a plebiscite, was attacked by the fascist Croatia." And further on, in the last paragraph, you say that: "The government of Krajina does not agree with the name used for part of Yugoslavia's state territory in these two documents that were being considered."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Three documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: And then the text continues on page 5: "Namely, what was called the Socialist Republic of Croatia is today the Serb Autonomous Region of Krajina as an independent political subject, and other Serb autonomous regions and the Republic of Croatia." Is that what is written here, Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Further on on page 5, under 832 - those are the last three digits - it says that: "The government supports the cease-fire in terms of all the provisions of that agreement, and the territory where the fighting is taking place is being called the Republic of Croatia." And at the end of this second paragraph on page 5, you say that: "The government of the SAO Krajina supports the cease-fire agreement because on its part it used fire and armed struggle only for the purposes of defence from Croatian aggression. And secondly, it believes in principle that all questions can and must be resolved by peaceful means only and democratic methods." In the next paragraph, number 3, you say: "Therefore, the government of the SAO Krajina requests that the government of the SAO Krajina be given the status of a host as was the case elsewhere in Yugoslavia, and that the government of the SAO Krajina warns all relevant factors that it is the only one to authorise monitor missions to stay in its territory." Is that what is written here, Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: At the end of this page 5, do you not say at the end, the last sentence, does it not read that: "The government of the SAO Krajina does not accept an insulting, an untenable treatment of the Serbian people as a national minority, which is what part of the European Community favours, as well as the neo-fascist Croat authorities supported by Vatican"? Is that what is written in the -- in this last sentence on page 5, Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Does it not say on page 6, in paragraph three from the top, that the government of SAO Krajina of course has nothing against the peace conference, but what it does not agree with is that the SAO Krajina is not being included in the -- or is not participating in the peace conference? And then in the last paragraph on page 6 you say that: "The government of the SAO Krajina, in relation to the position of the European Community, warns that -- excuse me, that the Peace Conference on Yugoslavia should not include the legal and legitimate organs of the SAO Krajina, warns both the European Community as well as the entire international community, or the international public, about the possible implications of such a position, because no decision by the Peace Conference on Yugoslavia will be binding on SAO Krajina unless it, too, does not fully participate in that conference." Is this what it states on page 6, Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does state that, but nobody actually took that into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, they did not. Let's move to page 7. At the top of the page, does it not state: "Since this question -- since we consider this question as important for our peace as well as for peace in Yugoslavia and Europe, we warn the responsible factors in Europe and in Yugoslavia to take into account this elementary political and legal fact in their concepts on the essential resolution of the Yugoslav state and political crisis and in halting the armed conflicts." Further on, in paragraph 2 on page 7, you say that: "The government of the SAO Krajina does not have the mandate of the Serbian people of SAO Krajina to make any kind of concessions to the detriment of the people who have given it their trust and confidence, and that is why we demand all the relevant factors in the process of deciding on peace in Yugoslavia to prevent violence over the Serb people of SAO Krajina being implemented by fascist Croatian authorities be substituted for another kind of violence which would then eradicate or erase the democratically expressed will of the Serbian people and thereby its right to self-determination." And your last sentence states: "For Serbian people to be free it means to be sovereign, and to be sovereign it means to exist in the form of one's own democratic state." Is this what it states at the end of this text on page 7, and did you, as the president of the government, sign this text, Mr. Babic?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Was this text sent to the United Nations and to all of these institutions, the Ministerial Council of the European Community, the parliament, and the High Commissioner of the OSCE? You did hand this text to all of these institutions?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, can you explain to us what is the truth now: What you wrote then in such detail on these seven pages, what you signed and sent to all the international institutions, or what you are telling us now over these past two days, which is completely opposite to what you have stated in this text?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this document is evidently full of very bombastic vocabulary terms. It's a politically powerful or politically charged text in which the international community is being asked to recognise the legitimacy of the government. This is being requested of the European Community, which was in the process of resolving the Yugoslav crisis. This was sent a little bit before the arrival of Mr. Henri Wijnaendts and before the preparations for negotiations, but this was not fruitful. So this vocabulary was adopted to the given situation, and it is a little bit over the top. So the response to your question is that this is over the top.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, I was asking you whether if it is true what you wrote to the United Nations, to the Council of Ministers of the European Union, to the parliament of the European Community, to the OSCE High Commission, or whether what you are telling us today in your testimony is true, and which is completely opposite. So what is true; what you said then or what you are saying now?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you about this text. The text is exaggerated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Babic, these organs of the international community which you addressed here, did they have any reason to believe you and did they believe you?

utterances.speaker: MILAN BABIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they didn't believe me then because the situation was different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: We just have one minute left. You were free, at liberty then. You were a president -- the president of the government. You were the minister of defence at that time. At that time you were the president of the municipality of Knin. You were a member of the SDS Main Board at that time. At that time you were a collocutor of international observers. Were you deceiving them at that time or today, as a person who is in prison, you are deceiving this Trial Chamber? What is true? You are telling two truths, Mr. Babic. You refuse to answer my question. I asked you is it true what is written here in the text or is it true what you are telling us here now?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may object to the form of the question. The document is quite lengthy and it contains a number of assertions which Mr. Milovancevic took a lot of time to go through. It seems to me that asking then at the end is this true in the broad, global, general sense is not particularly fruitful. If perhaps counsel were to address specifics in the document, specific assertions, the witness could address them more fruitfully [Realtime transcript read "truthfully"] rather than repeating this question again and again, which the witness has tried to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I suggest that we finish our work today, because we are running out of time, and I would like to tell the -- my friend from the Prosecution that tomorrow I'm going to deal with each single point from his objection, and I plan to cover each one of the points that he raised today. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That would be very helpful, Mr. Milovancevic. Mr. Milovancevic, seeing that you have read this whole document into the record, I assume you're not asking for the document to be admitted into evidence. Or what do you want us to do with this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you for reminding me of that. I would like to tender this document as a Defence exhibit. I was reading out the text in order to save time so that I would not have the witness read the document. It was important for me that the witness confirms the authenticity of each paragraph. But from what I hear from my colleagues from the Defence, this document is already admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure, but in the interests of brevity and expediency, reading the document when you are going to ask that it be admitted into evidence is not saving time, it is actually wasting time, Mr. Milovancevic. If you are going to tender it, you can put your questions on the document as it is because we can all read it. May I suggest that in the future let's try and save time. If you are going to tender the document, tender it and ask your questions. If you want to read it, read it and let somebody who is going to be writing the judgement not have the burden of reading the document in the record and as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I know we're overtime, just there is a correction I need to make on the transcript. On page 97, at line 24, it has me saying that the witness -- for the witness to address them more truthfully. I said more fruitfully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, I did hear you say "fruitfully." May the record show that the word "truthfully" should read "fruitfully."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOVANCEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, just one sentence. This situation will not occur very often during cross-examination. This is a very specific and extremely important document, so the Defence felt that it was in its interest that the Trial Chamber goes through each paragraph of the document together with the witness. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milovancevic. The observation of the Chamber is that in fact this was not an exceptional situation. It has been happening quite often, and again in the interests of expediency, you are requested to please try and help save time. Court stands adjourned to tomorrow at quarter past two in the afternoon in the same court. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 3rd day of March, 2006, at 2.15 p.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 7.06 p.m.,
